thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'cedar-ded-5' experiencing extreme tail latency and queued requests. Tenant implicated: humbolt-enterprises (VPC-dedicated). Start 2026-03-15T09:46Z. Paging marta_oncall.

marta_oncall: got the page, joining. I see large TCP retransmit spikes and request queue growth on the pool ingress. Some pods report p99 latency > 12s and steady 504s.

rachel_ops: joining. initial quick action: cordon node cedar-io-2 and throttle tenant ingress. running: 
```bash
redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant humbolt-enterprises --ingress-qps 20
redwoodctl node cordon cedar-io-2 --reason "net-saturation investigation"
```

devon_se: humbolt said they kicked off a large asset upload + concurrent evals earlier. Could be egress/ingress saturation on the host NIC causing writeback stalls. grabbing interface stats.

marta_oncall: netdev stats show TX drops and kernel tx queues full on cedar-io-2 nic eth0, offload counters high. NVMe writeback also spiking; I see iowait climbing. logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:47:02Z kernel: eth0: tx queue full, drop
2026-03-15T09:47:15Z runtime: request_queue_depth 342 -> 1204
2026-03-15T09:48:01Z kube: pod cedar-api-7 CrashLoopBackOff (throttled writes)
```

deploy-bot: recommended mitigation: drain-heavy-io -> fallback-route 'cedar-fallback-eu' available. Suggest gradual traffic shift 0%->30% over 90s.

ops_manager_tom: priority order: 1) protect other tenants (throttle & isolate), 2) shift heavy humbolt evals to fallback region, 3) investigate nic/kernel/iowait. CSM loop in.

csm_maya: pinging Humbolt contact (ops@humbolt.com). Draft message: 
"We detected elevated request failures and latency in your dedicated pool. We've throttled ingestion, isolated your workload to limit blast radius, and are shifting heavy jobs to a fallback pool. We'll share timeline and next steps ASAP."

rachel_ops: applied a temporary ingress cap and created an exception to route humbolt's long-running evals to fallback: 
```json
{"route_override": "cedar-fallback-eu", "max_ingress_qps": 20, "move_long_jobs": true}
```

eng-bot: fallback route activation task started (task id fh-4529). ETA ~2m. Canary 10% -> 100% in 3m.

marta_oncall: after canary traffic moved, observed request queue depth fall to ~120 and p99 latency back to ~400ms. But cedar-io-2 still showing elevated writeback. scheduling immediate kernel perf capture.

devon_se: grabbed perf data and a blktrace dump. dumping to S3: /s3/incidents/RED-INC-20260315-441/blktrace/humbolt-io-090946.tar.gz

ops_manager_tom: for handoffs: Marta retains mitigation ownership for 45m then pass to nate_oncall. Rachel to own infra RCA. Devon owns runtime/network tracing. CSM Maya owns customer comms & exec sync prep. Finance/Legal on standby for credits.

csm_maya: humbolt replied asking if this counts as SLA breach and requesting exec-level update if impact > 30m. They asked for a named engineer for postmortem — tagging devon_se + rachel_ops.

marta_oncall: timeline so far: 
- 09:46Z: heavy workload begins (client-side bulk evals)
- 09:47Z: net TX queue full, ingress queue grows, p50->p99 spike
- 09:48Z: tenant throttled + node cordoned
- 09:50Z: fallback route promoted, traffic shifted -> latency improvement
Containment window ~4 minutes to fallback stabilization; partial customer impact window 09:46-10:12Z while we monitored and validated.

rachel_ops: persisting logs and capturing host diagnostics. investigating whether host NIC driver/multiqueue config caused queue backpressure. preliminary fix candidates: enable IRQ-affinity, raise netdev tx ring, and enforce per-tenant egress quotas.

eng-bot: created follow-ups: INF-2275 per-tenant egress quotas, NET-301 tx-ring autotune, FALLBACK-129 faster cross-region route promotion.

ops_manager_tom: suggested credit guidance: Humbolt impacted window appears ~26 minutes (<30m threshold). propose a modest token credit (5%) with commitment to infra fixes + exec call. CSM to confirm if they still want exec sync.

csm_maya: Humbolt requested exec sync despite <30m impact. proposing 15:30 PDT. Also requested 2-hour named engineering deep-dive — scheduling devon and rachel. Will send interim note with timeline and proposed credit.

marta_oncall: added notes to incident doc and saved perf traces. retention extended for humbolt logs to 60 days. Pushed a non-blocking sysctl change on cedar-io-2 to increase net.core.netdev_max_backlog.

nate_oncall: on deck, will pick this up in 45m. please leave any monitoring queries in oncall doc.

devon_se: runtime finding: client opened many long-lived connections with small writes causing bufferbloat when NIC tx queues saturated; recommend client-side backpressure + server-side max-concurrency for streaming writes. Adding client guidance to postmortem.

csm_maya: interim sent to Humbolt with timeline, mitigations, and proposed credit. They accepted exec sync and asked for mitigations list.

ops_manager_tom: agreed to target interim RCA + credit recommendation by 15:30 PDT, full RCA by EOD tomorrow. Rachel + Devon to own RCA sections. Finance please standby.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=medium, mitigation_summary="tenant throttled, heavy jobs routed to fallback region, host network backlog tuned, diagnostics captured". Ticket RED-INC-20260315-441 created and linked to INF-2275, NET-301, FALLBACK-129.

eng-bot: preservation notes: retained perf traces and blktrace to S3, increased Humbolt log retention to 90 days.

rachel_ops: preliminary infra RCA notes: root cause is combined client-side bulk streaming pattern + insufficient per-tenant egress limits and host NIC queue config. Remediations: per-tenant egress quotas, NIC autotune, fallback promotion improvements, and client guidance for streaming workloads.

ops_manager_tom: reconvene in 40m for pre-exec sync. If anything changes reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
